info.title: Meridian Plugin API
info.description:
Interface of a remote HTTP plugin for Meridian (github.com/neria-cloud/meridian).
A plugin is a plain HTTP server; the host calls it with JSON messages. It
implements the same hooks as an in-process plugin and is addressed by name
with the same lifecycle (Capabilities, Init, GetName, Cleanup).

## Operations

Every hook is `POST /api/meridian/plugin/v1/{method}` (the method name in
lower case) with the request message as JSON body and the response message
as JSON reply. Hook-level failures are carried inside the response
(`error: HookError`); HTTP status codes are reserved for transport failures.

## HookStream (WebSocket)

`GET /api/meridian/plugin/v1/hookstream` upgrades to a WebSocket. Each
binary frame from the host is one `HookStreamRequest`, each frame from the
plugin one `HookStreamResponse` with the same `id`. The envelope carries
every hook above plus the lifecycle calls; exactly one payload property is
set per message, and `call` names it. OpenAPI cannot describe WebSocket
frames natively, so the operation documents them with the `x-websocket`
extension. Meridian calls every hook over the stream; the POST operations
stay for tooling and for `Capabilities`, which the host sends first.

## Parity and body_changed

Message properties are the JSON tags of Meridian's core structs (HTTPRequest,
HTTPResponse, BifrostError, the typed Bifrost<Type>Request/Response named by
`request_type`); untagged core unions cross as a discriminator plus the
typed struct's JSON. Every reply carries `body_changed`: false (default)
tells the host to keep its objects untouched and skip decoding any payload
in the reply; true makes the reply's payload replace them in place.

## Validation

All schemas are plain JSON Schema 2020-12 (OpenAPI 3.1). The Go package
`framework/pluginshttp` of Meridian is generated from this document
(`bifrost-prep genspec`) and is the client-side view of the same contract.

get.description:
Upgrades the connection to a WebSocket. Afterwards every binary frame
from the host is one `HookStreamRequest` and every binary frame from the
plugin one `HookStreamResponse` with the same `id`, in order. The host
keeps one stream per concurrent caller; there is no interleaving of
requests on one stream.

The `enc` query parameter selects the JSON encoder the plugin should use
for its replies.

parameters.name: enc
parameters.description: JSON encoding of the frames (informational for the plugin; both are the same JSON)

101.description: Switching Protocols; the connection now carries WebSocket binary frames

404.description: Wrong path (the plugin only serves the upgrade on this path)

x-websocket.description: One binary frame per message, no fragmentation semantics beyond RFC 6455; client-to-server frames are masked

PluginBearerAuth.description:
Optional. The host sends the headers the operator configured for the plugin (for example
Authorization: Bearer <token>) on the HookStream upgrade, on POST /capabilities and on the
health/status probes; the plugin decides whether to require them.

TransportError.description: Transport-level failure (unknown method, malformed message, plugin shutting down). Hook-level errors never use this; they travel inside the response message.

ContextDetails.description:
Wire projection of the host's request context (host -> plugin): request id,
deadline and the string-valued context entries. The plugin rebuilds a local
context from it and returns its writes as a ContextDelta.

request_id.description: Request identifier (also present in ContextDetails.values under the request-id key)

deadline_unix_nano.description: Absolute deadline as Unix nanoseconds; 0 = no deadline

values.description:
Context values whose key is a BifrostContextKey. Any JSON value (string, number, boolean,
array, object); credentials (direct provider key, session token, raw virtual key) never cross.

plugin_scope.description: Name of the plugin the context is scoped to

ContextDelta.description: Context writes made by the plugin during a call (plugin -> host); the host merges them into the real context

set.description: Keys to set (or overwrite); any JSON value. Reserved host keys are dropped by the host.

RequestDetails.description:
HTTP transport request envelope: exactly the JSON tags of Meridian's
core schemas.HTTPRequest (method, path, headers, query, path_params, body)
plus host extras. Carried by the HTTPTransport* hooks; LLM/MCP hooks carry
LLMRequest / MCPRequest instead.

The body appears in exactly one of two forms: `body` (raw JSON, used when the
request body is valid JSON, copied verbatim) or `body_b64` (base64, used for
any other content).

path_params.description: Path variables extracted from the URL pattern

body.description: Request body as raw JSON (any JSON value); present only when the body is valid JSON

body_b64.description: Request body, base64-encoded; present only when the body is not valid JSON

received_at_unix_nano.description: When the host received the request, Unix nanoseconds

ResponseDetails.description:
HTTP transport response envelope: exactly the JSON tags of Meridian's core
schemas.HTTPResponse (status_code, headers, body). `body` is raw JSON when the
body is valid JSON, `body_b64` (base64) otherwise.

body.description: Response body as raw JSON (any JSON value); present only when the body is valid JSON

body_b64.description: Response body, base64-encoded; present only when the body is not valid JSON

StreamChunk.description:
One streamed unit. `chunk` is the JSON of Meridian's core schemas.BifrostStreamChunk
(its MarshalJSON: the one non-nil embedded stream response for `request_type`, or a
BifrostError chunk recognisable by `is_bifrost_error`). `index` is host-assigned, 0-based,
per request.

BifrostError.description:
Meridian's core schemas.BifrostError with its JSON tags verbatim (event_id, type,
is_bifrost_error, status_code, error, extra_fields). `allow_fallbacks` and
`stream_control` are json:"-" in Go and made explicit here because plugins control them.
It is data, not a transport failure.

allow_fallbacks.description: Boolean; controls fallback behaviour. Absent = the host keeps its own value (default allowed).

RequestType.description: schemas.RequestType; the value names the typed core request/response carried next to it

LLMRequest.description:
An LLM-side request: `request_type` names the typed core request and `request` is that
struct's own JSON (schemas.BifrostChatRequest for chat_completion(_stream), schemas.BifrostEmbeddingRequest
for embedding, ...). The untagged union schemas.BifrostRequest is never marshalled.

request.description: JSON of schemas.Bifrost<Type>Request for request_type (any JSON value)

LLMResponse.description: An LLM-side response; `response` is the JSON of schemas.Bifrost<Type>Response for `request_type`

LLMShortCircuit.description: Mirrors schemas.LLMPluginShortCircuit; exactly one of response / error is expected

MCPRequest.description:
An MCP request: the untagged schemas.BifrostMCPRequest crosses as `request_type`, `client_name`
(snake_case of the Go fields) and `request` = JSON of the typed core MCP request.

request.description: JSON of the typed schemas.BifrostMCP<Type>Request (any JSON value)

MCPResponse.description: An MCP response; `response` is the JSON of schemas.BifrostMCPResponse

MCPConnectRequest.description: schemas.BifrostMCPConnectRequest (untagged in Go; snake_case of the Go field names)

extra.description: Remaining fields of the Go struct as a JSON object (any JSON value)

HookError.description: The Go `error` returned by a hook. Absent means nil. Distinct from transport failures.

ConfigMap.description: A plugin configuration object: free-form JSON, passed through unchanged.

Trace.description: schemas.Trace handed to ObservabilityPlugin.Inject (full shape, spans included)

HookName.description: Name of a hook (an operation of this document)

TransportErrorBody.description: Body of a transport-level failure (the plugin could not run the call at all)

CapabilitiesResponse.description: Which hooks the plugin implements and its protocol version

hooks.description: Implemented hooks; the host never calls a hook that is not listed

protocol_version.description: Wire protocol version; the host refuses anything but the version it speaks (currently 1)

stream_supported.description: True when the plugin serves HookStream

InitRequest.description: Plugin configuration, passed once after Capabilities

CleanupRequest.description: Empty request; sent once before the host stops the plugin process

HealthResponse.description: Mirrors Meridian's /health; 200 for ok/degraded, 503 for unavailable

StatusResponse.description: Identity, capabilities and counters of the plugin process

version.description: Build version of the plugin, free-form

HTTPTransportPreHookResponse.description:
Output of the transport pre-hooks. `response` set = short-circuit with that
response; `request` echoes the (possibly mutated) request so the host can
apply in-place semantics; `ctx` carries context writes; `error` is the
hook's Go error.

body_changed.description:
false (or absent): the host keeps the request/response/error/chunk it already holds and does not
decode any payload carried by this reply; omit the payload to save bytes. true: the payload
properties of this reply replace the host's objects in place; an absent property then means nil
(empty body, recovered error, dropped chunk). Transport metadata of an echoed request/response
(method, path, headers, query, path_params, status_code) is applied whenever the echo object is
present, independent of this flag.

decode any payload carried by this reply; omit the payload to save bytes. true: the payload
properties of this reply replace the host's objects in place; an absent property then means nil
(empty body, recovered error, dropped chunk). Transport metadata of an echoed request/response
(method, path, headers, query, path_params, status_code) is applied whenever the echo object is
present, independent of this flag.

chunk.description: The (possibly mutated) chunk; absent with body_changed=true = drop the chunk

false (or absent): the host keeps the request/response/error/chunk it already holds and does not
decode any payload carried by this reply; omit the payload to save bytes. true: the payload
properties of this reply replace the host's objects in place; an absent property then means nil
(empty body, recovered error, dropped chunk). Transport metadata of an echoed request/response
(method, path, headers, query, path_params, status_code) is applied whenever the echo object is
present, independent of this flag.

PreRequestHookResponse.description: PreRequestHook cannot short-circuit; its error is non-blocking (logged by the host)

body_changed.description:
false (or absent): the host keeps the request/response/error/chunk it already holds and does not
decode any payload carried by this reply; omit the payload to save bytes. true: the payload
properties of this reply replace the host's objects in place; an absent property then means nil
(empty body, recovered error, dropped chunk). Transport metadata of an echoed request/response

PreLLMHookResponse.description:
`request` is the (possibly mutated) request, applied only when `body_changed` is true.
`short_circuit` stops the pipeline with a response or an error.

body_changed.description:
false (or absent): the host keeps the request/response/error/chunk it already holds and does not
decode any payload carried by this reply; omit the payload to save bytes. true: the payload
properties of this reply replace the host's objects in place; an absent property then means nil
(empty body, recovered error, dropped chunk). Transport metadata of an echoed request/response
(method, path, headers, query, path_params, status_code) is applied whenever the echo object is
present, independent of this flag.

PostLLMHookRequest.description: Post-hooks receive the provider response and/or the provider error; no request (the LLMPlugin signature)

PostLLMHookResponse.description: With body_changed=true BOTH response and plugin_error replace the host's (absent = nil, i.e. a recovered error)

body_changed.description:
false (or absent): the host keeps the request/response/error/chunk it already holds and does not
decode any payload carried by this reply; omit the payload to save bytes. true: the payload
properties of this reply replace the host's objects in place; an absent property then means nil
(empty body, recovered error, dropped chunk). Transport metadata of an echoed request/response
(method, path, headers, query, path_params, status_code) is applied whenever the echo object is
present, independent of this flag.
false = keep the host's request (payload not decoded); true = `request` replaces it
false = keep the host's response and error; true = both are replaced by this reply (absent = nil)
false = keep the host's request; true = the mutable fields (connection_string, headers) are replaced
false = keep the host's response and error; true = both are replaced by this reply (absent = nil)

InjectRequest.description: A completed trace. `ctx` carries only request id and deadline (Inject takes a plain context)

HookStreamRequest.description:
One host -> plugin message on the stream. `id` is echoed in the reply.
Exactly one payload property is present and `call` names it. The lifecycle
calls use the same envelope.

id.description: Per-stream sequence number, unique among in-flight requests on this stream

call.description: Name of the call carried in this message

HookStreamResponse.description:
One plugin -> host message. `id` matches the request. Either exactly one
payload property is present (the call's response message) or
`transport_error` explains why the call could not be dispatched at all
(unknown call, decode failure, plugin shutting down).

call.description: Name of the call this message answers (informational)
